## File: `AGENTS.md`

# AGENTS.md

Canonical instructions for every coding agent working in `pauli-contextuality-lab` (Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor, Grok Build, Grok Bot, and others).
`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursor/rules/build-standard.mdc`, and `llms.txt` only point here. Edit this file, never the pointers.
Full standard: `docs/build-standard.md` (Build Standard for LLMs v1.2.0, 90 items).

## Project

- **Name:** Pauli Contextuality Lab (`pauli-contextuality-lab`)
- **Purpose:** Unified Lean 4.35.0 (Mathlib v4.35.0) and exact-arithmetic verification repository for three Pauli contextuality research tracks:
  1. `tracks/spectral-bounds/` (`lean/HoggarBound/`): Spectral floor (Hoggar/Kramers bound), floor-saturating states including the infinite pure-CCZ determinant family `|Psi_{3m}>`, classical N=4..5 ladders, exact four-qubit C3 binary optima (`368` vs `344`), and Jonah's Conjecture E across all nine vertex cases for every `N >= 4`.
  2. `tracks/disjoint-mermin/` (`lean/ContextualityTensor/`): Exact contextuality degrees `d_k = (7^k - 5^k)/2` (`k` disjoint Peres-Mermin squares) and `(6^k - 4^k)/2` (`k` Mermin pentagrams), answering Section 6 of Muller & Saniga (`arXiv:2609.19862v1`).
  3. `tracks/sequential-evidence/` (`lean/Evidence/`): Exact finite-tree sequential contextuality evidence bounds and constructive setting-bias attack on the Peres-Mermin square (`97.24%` naive vs `0.89%` corrected false rejection at nominal `1%`).
- **Author:** Alexander S. Donahue (independent researcher, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`, `0_0@0thernes.art`)
- **Licenses:** `Apache-2.0` (`LICENSE`, all code) + `CC-BY-4.0` (`LICENSE-DOCS`, all papers/docs/figures) + MIT for vendored `third_party/` (`NOTICE`)
- **Manifest:** `repo.yaml` (schema: `repo-standard.schema.json`), `formalization.yaml` (Palomar-compatible Lean provenance)
- **Status:** Active research preprints — NOT externally peer reviewed; AI-assisted under human direction.

## Layout

- `lean/`: Single unified Lean 4.35.0 + Mathlib v4.35.0 package (`HoggarBound`, `ContextualityTensor`, `Evidence`, `Challenge`, `Solution`, `VerifyAll`, `comparator.json`).
- `tracks/`: Track-specific C11 engines, Python exact verifiers, interactive browser labs (`web/`), and checked JSON receipts (`results/`).
- `papers/`: Publication manuscripts (`spectral-bounds/`, `disjoint-mermin/`, `sequential-evidence/`), PDFs, LaTeX sources, BibTeX, and correspondence guide.
- `data/`: Witness hex masks, flat-state supports, and `data/MANIFEST.sha256`.
- `third_party/`: Single deduplicated vendored Tsotchke stack (`moonlab/`, `qgtl/`, `quantum_rng/`, `SHA256SUMS.json`).
- `blueprint/`: Lean Blueprint LaTeX (`blueprint/src/content.tex`) + declaration-checked dependency graph builder.
- `scripts/`: Unified verification (`verify_all.py`), Blueprint builder (`build_blueprint.py`), static site builder (`build_site.py`), citation/axiom/arithmetic audits, and Build Standard v1.2.0 auditors (`audit-repo.sh`, `Audit-Repo.ps1`).
- `tests/`: Automated Python (exact, Hypothesis property, negative, mutation/fuzz, integrity) and Node.js test suites.
- `docs/`: Architecture, ADRs, statement-fidelity table, threat model, operations, FAQ, glossary, run log, and 10-pass review logs.

## Commands

Run via `just <recipe>` or `bash scripts/dev.sh <recipe>`:

- `just setup`: Install pinned Python dependencies (`requirements.txt`) and fetch pinned Mathlib cache (`lean/`).
- `just build`: Build all three Lean libraries (`HoggarBound`, `ContextualityTensor`, `Evidence`) and compile C11 verifiers with `-Wall -Wextra`.
- `just test`: Run the unified Python (`pytest`) and Node (`node --test`) verification suites across all 3 tracks.
- `just lint`: Run `ruff`, `mypy`, C compiler warnings, and Batteries `lake exe runLinter` (report-only).
- `just sanitizers`: Compile and execute C11 engines under `-fsanitize=address,undefined`.
- `just verify-lean`: Build Lean modules, run exhaustive `#print axioms` audit (`VerifyAll.lean`), check zero forbidden tokens, and run 6-kernel `lake comparator --config comparator.json --paranoid`.
- `just blueprint`: Validate every `\lean{...}` declaration in `blueprint/src/content.tex` and build the dependency graph.
- `just site`: Assemble the unified GitHub Pages portal (`build/site/`) including all 3 browser labs, papers, and `/blueprint/`.
- `just reproduce`: Clean-clone end-to-end exact verification + audits + blueprint + site assembly.
- `just audit`: Score this repository against Build Standard v1.2.0 (`scripts/audit-repo.sh` / `scripts/Audit-Repo.ps1`).
- `just release X.Y.Z`: Bump `VERSION`, update `CHANGELOG.md`/`CITATION.cff`, tag `vX.Y.Z`, and push straight to `main`.

## Hard Rules (Build Standard v1.2.0)

- **R1.** Nothing may gate, block, or slow a commit or push. No branch protection, no required status checks, no commit/tag signing requirements, no git hooks, no push protection, no merge queues, no coverage/lint/SAST/SBOM gates.
- **R2.** Commit and push straight to `main`. No pull requests and no feature branches.
- **R3.** CI is informational. Failures are findings fixed in follow-up commits to `main`.
- **R4.** Banned tools/files: no Dependabot/Renovate, no PR templates, no CodeRabbit, no Copilot review or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, no `FUNDING.yml`.
- **R5.** One-person lean, not corporate. Prefer one file over a framework, one command over a checklist.
- **R6.** Never fabricate. Every number, claim, axiom output, badge, and test result must come from a real run of current code.
- **R7.** Classify every finding as exactly one of the 10 classes: `bug`, `error`, `issue`, `problem`, `concern`, `dilemma`, `conflict`, `gap`, `hole`, `blindspot` (definitions in `docs/glossary.md`).
- **R8.** Precedence: Owner's explicit instruction > Hard Rules > Build Standard items > ecosystem conventions.

## Known Traps

- **`lean/Challenge.lean` intentional `sorry` stubs:** `Challenge.lean` contains `sorry` ONLY as the isolated statement-only specification checked against sorry-free `Solution.lean` by `lake comparator --config comparator.json --paranoid`. Never put `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide`, or custom `axiom` in any proof module or `Solution.lean`.
- **Single GitHub Pages site:** `.github/workflows/pages.yml` deploys `build/site/` assembled by `scripts/build_site.py`, mounting `/blueprint/` alongside all three interactive browser labs and papers. Never add a second Pages workflow.
- **PowerShell bracket safety on Windows:** On the author's ReFS Dev Drive (`Z:\[Vibe Coded (AI)]\...`), always use `-LiteralPath` in PowerShell file cmdlets.
- **Honest affiliation & scope:** Always use `Alexander S. Donahue (independent researcher)` (never assert an unformed LLC). Never claim external peer review, journal acceptance, arXiv submission, or Palomar registration unless genuinely completed.

## File: `CLAIMS.md`

# Claims & Falsification Ledger (`CLAIMS.md`)

Every headline claim in `pauli-contextuality-lab` is tagged with its exact verification status (`kernel-checked`, `certificate-checked`, `paper proof`, `numerical_approximation`, or `open`), its relation to earlier work, and an explicit falsification condition (Build Standard items B04 & B42).

**Kernel coverage.** `kernel-checked` means checked by the Lean 4.35.0 kernel (`lake build`, `#print axioms` in `lean/VerifyAll.lean`, standard axioms only). Only the 12 comparator targets in `lean/comparator.json` (Targets 1–12 below) and their dependency closure were also accepted by 6 independent kernels via `lake comparator --paranoid`. Nine Track 1 modules (`Saturated*`, `C3Certificate`, `C3Spectra`, `C3Theorem`, `FlatData`, `PhaseData`) are not compiled by CI at `v3.1.0`; claims that rest on them are marked below.

**Statement audit.** The wording below was corrected on 2026-11-26 to match an independent statement audit ([audit log](https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md)); see [ERRATA.md](ERRATA.md).

| ID | Track | Claim | Evidence Tag | Relation to Literature | Verification Artifact | What Would Prove Us Wrong (Falsifier) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C01** | Track 1 | Universal spectral floor $(D-1)\beta_6(S,f) \le (D-2)\lvert S\rvert\sqrt{(D-1)\lvert S\rvert}$ for all $N \ge 1$ and $S \subseteq W(2N-1,2)$ | `kernel-checked` | Formalization of Jonah's prior result (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.23538829`, unreviewed), here for arbitrary supports | `lean/HoggarBound/Bound.lean` (`hoggar_bound`), `Challenge.lean` Target 1 | Exhibiting any $N$-qubit Pauli set $S$ and $\pm 1$ assignment violating the inequality, or a non-standard axiom in `VerifyAll.lean`. |
| **C02** | Track 1 | Quaternionic / Kramers spectral floor ($n = D/2$) on $Q^-(2N-1,2)$ giving $d(Q^-(5,2))\ge 9$, $d(Q^-(7,2))\ge 291$, $d(Q^-(9,2))\ge 6501$ | `kernel-checked` | Formalization of Jonah's prior result (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.23538829`) | `lean/HoggarBound/Kramers.lean` (`hoggar_bound_quaternionic`), Target 2 | Any assignment on $Q^-(2N-1,2)$ beating the Kramers bound or violating antiunitary commutation. |
| **C03** | Track 1 | Small degrees: $d(Q^+(3,2))=1$, $d(W(5,2))=63$, $d(Q^-(5,2))=9$, and $2 \le d(W(3,2)) \le 3$ | `kernel-checked` (standard kernel; not comparator targets) | Known values, here formalized (anchors in `docs/statement-fidelity.md`); $d(W(3,2))$ is not determined exactly | `lean/HoggarBound/TwoQubit.lean`, `Witness.lean` (`mermin_peres`, `degree_three_qubit`, `degree_three_qubit_elliptic`) | Any assignment violating $<63$ contexts in $W(5,2)$, $<9$ in $Q^-(5,2)$, or $0$ in $Q^+(3,2)$. |
| **C04** | Track 1 | For every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $N$, every $\pm 1$ assignment violates more than a $(1/2 - \varepsilon)$ fraction of flags on $W(2N-1,2)$ and on $Q^-(2N-1,2)$ (lower direction only). The matching upper bound and the $Q^+$ case are paper arguments; `hyperbolic_fraction_tendsto_half` is a limit of a closed-form expression and mentions no assignment. | `kernel-checked` (lower direction, $W$ and $Q^-$) + `paper proof` (upper direction, $Q^+$) | Follows from Jonah's floor | `lean/HoggarBound/AuditUpgrades.lean` (`full_space_violated_fraction_eventually_gt`, `elliptic_violated_fraction_eventually_gt`) | A sequence of assignments whose violated fraction stays bounded below $1/2 - \varepsilon$. |
| **C05** | Track 1 | Five-way saturation equivalence (`saturation_tfae`) and squareness $(2^N-1)\lvert S\rvert = \square$ | `kernel-checked` | Jonah's preprint states an attainment criterion for closed families that overlaps the equivalence (not compared line by line); squareness is an elementary corollary ($\beta_6$ is an integer) | `lean/HoggarBound/SaturationTheory.lean`, Target 3 | A floor-saturating set with $(2^N-1)\lvert S\rvert$ non-square or no flat pure state. |
| **C06** | Track 1 | Infinite family of non-closed pure-CCZ Pauli sets $\lvert\Psi_{3m}\rangle$ attaining the spectral floor for all $m \ge 1$, contextual for $m \ge 2$ (the $m = 1$ member has degree 0); degree $2016$ at $m = 2$. The finite flat degrees $75, 480, 729344$ are in `Saturated*` modules that CI does not compile at `v3.1.0`. | `kernel-checked` (family, degree 2016); `open` at this release for $75, 480, 729344$ | New to a bounded search; the question was posed in this repository's own manuscript | `lean/HoggarBound/NormPhaseFamily.lean`, `SaturatedPhaseSix.lean` (`det6_degree`), `norm_phase_family.py` (32/32 checks), Target 4 | A counterexample $m \ge 2$ where support is closed or degree differs from $\frac{1}{12}(q^3-1)q^3(q-1)(q-2)$. |
| **C07** | Track 1 | For every $N \ge 4$ and one explicit representative $(X,d)$ of each of the 9 vertex cases of Jonah's Conjecture E, there are cospectral $\pm 1$ carriers whose completion matrices have different characteristic polynomials (strict-law failure; also for sorted eigenvalue lists). That each representative lies in its named case (labels are Lean comments) and transfer to every hyperplane of a case (Jonah [J3, Thm B4]) are outside Lean. | `kernel-checked` (one representative per case) + cited paper input (Theorem B4) | Answers Jonah's Conjecture E (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.23524332`, unreviewed, AI-refereed) for one representative per case; Jonah already proved cases C1 and C6 | `lean/HoggarBound/ConjectureE.lean`, `AuditUpgrades.lean`, `conjecture_e_trace_formula.py` (136 checks), Target 6 | A case among the 9 where the constructed carrier pair is not cospectral or has identical completion spectra, or a representative that does not lie in its named case. |
| **C08** | Track 1 | For one fixed four-qubit Case C3 sign pair $(\sigma_0, \sigma_1)$: $\min_y F(\sigma_0,y) = 368$ and $\min_y F(\sigma_1,y) = 344$ over binary completions $y$. The cospectrality of the pair is proved in `C3Certificate.lean` / `C3Theorem.lean`, which CI does not compile at `v3.1.0`. | `kernel-checked` (optima) | Self-posed bounded instance (single finite case) | `lean/HoggarBound/C3ExactOptima.lean`, `c3_exact_optima_check.py` (10/10 checks), Target 5 | Any binary vector $y \in \{\pm 1\}^{64}$ giving $<368$ for $\sigma_0$ or $<344$ for $\sigma_1$. |
| **C09** | Track 1 | Lower bounds $d(W(7,2)) \ge 1455$ and $d(Q^+(9,2)) \ge 6444$; CSS witnesses $(315, 1575, 6975)$; reduction of the exact values $1575, 6975$ to $d(Q^-(7,2)) \ge 315$ | `kernel-checked` (bounds, reduction) + `certificate-checked` (42-orbit census) | Jonah's unreviewed, computer-assisted note (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.23510634`, 20 Oct 2026) already claimed the exact values $1575$ and $6975$, which imply these bounds; this is an independent kernel-checked proof of the bounds. $1455$ raises the lower bound $1071$ of Li, Gupta and Ganesh (`arXiv:2610.26465`) for $W(7,2)$, and $6444 > 4743$ answers their question on $Q^+(9,2)$ negatively | `lean/HoggarBound/ExactDegreesN4N5.lean`, `w52_census_verify.c`, `exact_degrees_n4_n5.py` (9/9), Targets 7–8 | An assignment violating $<1455$ lines in $W(7,2)$ or $<315$ in $Q^-(7,2)$, or an orbit missed by the 42-orbit C census. |
| **C10** | Track 1 | Exhaustive $N=9$ cyclic-invariant rank-8 search finds 0 hits across 540,299,769 forms | `certificate-checked` (C census, outside Lean) | Self-posed computation | `tracks/spectral-bounds/src/n9_rank8_search.c`, `tracks/spectral-bounds/results/n9_rank8_search.tsv` | Exhibiting a cyclic-invariant cubic form on 9 qubits with constant rank 8. |
| **C11** | Track 2 | Exact degrees $d_k = (7^k - 5^k)/2$ ($k$ disjoint Peres-Mermin squares) and $(6^k - 4^k)/2$ ($k$ Mermin pentagrams) for the explicit union-context family (each nonempty choice of at most one signed line per copy), with $2d_k/L_k \to 1$ | `kernel-checked` (formulas; limit by the standard kernel only) + `certificate-checked` (identification of the Lean seed contexts with $HS(L(K_{3,3}))$ and $HS(\mathrm{Petersen})$ by Python enumeration) | Answers the stacking-limit question of Muller & Saniga (`arXiv:2609.19862v1`, Sec. 6, unreviewed preprint) for squares and pentagrams only; the context-count product formula is from their Sec. 4.2 | `lean/ContextualityTensor.lean`, `ActualModel.lean`, `tests/test_disjoint_mermin.py`, Targets 9–10 | Any deterministic assignment on $k$ disjoint blocks violating fewer than $(7^k - 5^k)/2$ (squares) or $(6^k - 4^k)/2$ (pentagrams) union contexts. |
| **C12** | Track 3 | Peres-Mermin setting-bias failure floor $\min_c p(c)$, finite betting-tree hitting bound $\le z/T$, and miscalibrated 1% test false-rejection probability $97.2443815\%$ vs $0.8907211\%$ at horizon 1,000 | `kernel-checked` (bounds & 36-step counterexample, $> 4.3\%$) + `certificate-checked` (exact rational 1,000-step DP & 18,000-trial replay) | Formalization of elementary known bounds (finite form of Ville's inequality; `papers/sequential-evidence/PRIOR_ART.md`) | `lean/Evidence/{Square,Sequential}.lean`, `tracks/sequential-evidence/scripts/verify_artifact.py`, `tests/test_sequential_evidence.py`, Targets 11–12 | A valid finite tree exceeding $z/T$ hitting probability, or a rational DP discrepancy against exhaustive path enumeration. |
| **C13** | All | Browser labs and Moonlab / QGTL / `quantum_rng` runs | `numerical_approximation` (classical simulation) | Not a research claim | `third_party/`, `results/arithmetic-audit.json` | Not a hardware quantum claim; falsified if simulator disagrees with exact analytical Pauli expectations beyond stated tolerance. |

## File: `LIMITATIONS.md`

# Limitations, Epistemic Boundaries, and AI-Contribution Disclosure

## 1. Real vs. Metaphor & What Is Not Claimed

- **Not externally peer reviewed:** All three manuscripts in `papers/` are unreviewed research preprints. Passing Lean 4 kernel checks certifies the logical validity of the formalized statements inside Lean — not external referee acceptance, historical priority, or statement-to-literature fidelity.
- **No quantum hardware measurements:** Moonlab (`third_party/moonlab/`) is a classical state-vector simulator compiled to WebAssembly; `quantum_rng` (`third_party/quantum_rng/`) is a seeded classical pseudorandom generator; QGTL (`third_party/qgtl/`) provides classical differential-geometry C kernels. Nothing in this repository is a physical experiment on quantum hardware or certified quantum randomness.
- **Prior work & unreviewed preprint citations:**
  - The spectral floor inequality, its Kramers variant and Conjecture E stem from unreviewed Zenodo preprints by B. W. Jonah (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.23538829`, `23510634`, `23524332`). The floors are Jonah's prior results; this repository formalizes them for arbitrary supports. Jonah's preprint `23538829` also states an attainment criterion for closed families that overlaps `saturation_tfae`. Jonah's computer-assisted note `23510634` (20 October 2026) already claimed the exact values $d(W(7,2)) = 1575$ and $d(Q^+(9,2)) = 6975$, which imply the kernel-checked lower bounds $1455$ and $6444$ proved here. The Conjecture E source is AI-assisted and AI-refereed; it already proves cases C1 and C6.
  - Symplectic polar-space degrees: Muller et al. (`arXiv:2407.02928`). The repeated-disjoint-copy question: A. Muller and M. Saniga (`arXiv:2609.19862v1`, an unreviewed arXiv v1 preprint). Their Sec. 4.2 gives the context-count product formula $|HS(G_1 \cup \dots \cup G_k)| = \prod_i (|HS(G_i)|+1) - 1$ used in Track 2. A. Cabello (`arXiv:1002.3135`, 2010) reports a related growth result, in which the violation grows exponentially with $n$.
  - $d(Q^+(7,2))=315$ is due to Li, Gupta, and Ganesh (`arXiv:2610.26465`); the numerical five-qubit flat state is due to Cieśliński (`arXiv:2610.07172`); the scalar skewness bound is Okumura (1974).
  - Concurrent independent work: a Zenodo deposit (`doi:10.5281/zenodo.24567331`, created 26 November 2026, after the v3.0.0 CI run) describes a floor-type lower bound, the $1/2$ limit, an exactness criterion for pure states with constant-modulus Pauli expectations, a five-qubit configuration of degree 480, and a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization. It is later than, not prior to, this release; the overlap has not been compared in detail.
  - Novelty claims (Track 1 Section 5 flat states and $|\Psi_{3m}\rangle$, Track 1 Conjecture E formalization, Track 2 arbitrary-$k$ closed forms) rest on bounded literature searches and do not claim exhaustive historical priority. The question answered by $|\Psi_{3m}\rangle$ was posed in this repository's own manuscript, not by another author.
- **Scope of the answers to external questions:**
  - Track 2 answers the stacking-limit question at the end of the second paragraph of Muller & Saniga, Sec. 6, for disjoint Peres–Mermin squares and Mermin pentagrams only. The two doily copies named in the same sentence, mixed unions and the other Sec. 6 outlooks are not treated. The source poses this as an open question in its discussion, not as a conjecture.
  - Track 1 proves strict-law failure for one explicit representative of each of the nine vertex cases of Conjecture E, for every $N \ge 4$. Case membership of each representative and transfer to whole cases (Jonah's Theorem B4) are outside Lean (Section 2).

## 2. Explicit Kernel Boundary (What Lies Outside Lean 4)

The following items are **not** certified by the Lean 4 kernel and are explicitly tagged as `certificate-checked`, `paper proof`, or `numerical_approximation` in `CLAIMS.md`:

1. **42-orbit `W(5,2)` census (`tracks/spectral-bounds/src/w52_census_verify.c`):** Exhaustive C11 enumeration (17,652,160 classes across 42 orbits) + pure-integer Python duals reproducing Jonah's $(315, 1575, 6975)$. Lean proves the exact master reduction (`exact_degrees_n4_n5_of_q7minus_315`) and the lower bounds `1455` and `6444` (which do not depend on the census), not the C orbit search itself. The exact values 1575 and 6975 hold in Lean only conditionally on $d(Q^-(7,2)) \ge 315$.
2. **Nine-qubit cyclic-symmetry rank-8 search (`n9_rank8_search.c`):** C11 enumeration of 540,299,769 forms (0 hits).
3. **Single-orbit transitivity input (`Jonah [J3, Theorem B4]`):** Cited paper input for transporting Conjecture E to arbitrary hyperplane classes outside our constructed representatives. The case labels (from Jonah's list C1–C16) of the nine Lean representatives appear only in comments in `lean/HoggarBound/ConjectureE.lean`; no Lean statement ties a representative to its case.
4. **Floating-point scripts:** Every Python file using `numpy` or floating-point arithmetic is automatically classified in `results/arithmetic-audit.json` (`scripts/arithmetic_audit.py`) and never relied upon for a formal proof.
5. **Physical assumptions of Track 3 (`Evidence`):** The finite adaptive-tree theorem assumes a true conditional setting floor $\beta$ and single context-independent value table per trial; no empirical transcript alone can certify those physical assumptions.
6. **Track 2 identification with the source's objects:** No Lean theorem identifies the hard-coded seed lines in `lean/ContextualityTensor.lean` with $HS(L(K_{3,3}))$ or $HS(\mathrm{Petersen})$; `lean/ContextualityTensor/Support.lean` is generic and not instantiated. The pentagram signs have no Pauli-matrix check in Lean, and `lean/ContextualityTensor/PhysicalBridge.lean` covers two squares only. The identification rests on Python enumeration and the source's Sec. 4.2. The six-kernel comparator targets 9–10 use the tuple-indexed model; the vertex-subset theorems (`global_actual_*`) and the limit theorems (`actual_*_epsilon_tends_to_one`) are checked by the standard Lean kernel only.
7. **Modules not compiled at `v3.1.0`:** CI and the default Lake targets do not compile `HoggarBound.Saturated`, `SaturatedFive`, `SaturatedPhaseFive`, `SaturatedPhaseSeven`, `C3Certificate`, `C3Spectra`, `C3Theorem`, `FlatData` and `PhaseData`. The finite flat degrees 75, 480 and 729344 and the cospectrality certificate of the C3 sign pair therefore have no compiled, axiom-audited evidence at this release; earlier runs were made in the archived `hoggar-bound-lab` repository.
8. **Six-kernel coverage:** Only the 12 comparator targets in `lean/comparator.json` and their dependency closure were accepted by the 6 independent kernels (`leanchecker-paranoid`, `lean4lean`, `nanoda`, `con-leche`, `con-ron`, `lean-default`). All other kernel-checked theorems are checked by the standard Lean kernel. The masked 300 s `leanchecker --fresh Evidence || true` step that produced no output before timeout in CI run `45826042676` was removed in `v3.1.0` so CI does not misreport it.
9. **Half-violation limit (`CLAIMS.md` C04):** Lean proves only the lower direction, for $W(2N-1,2)$ and $Q^-(2N-1,2)$; the upper direction and $Q^+(2N-1,2)$ are paper arguments.
10. **Human line-by-line statement fidelity audit:** `formalization.yaml` explicitly records `human_line_by_line_review_recorded: false` until an independent mathematician (or the author line-by-line) signs off on every row of `docs/statement-fidelity.md`.

## File: `docs/statement-fidelity.md`

# Statement-Fidelity Audit Table (`docs/statement-fidelity.md`)

Maps every headline Lean 4.35.0 declaration across all three tracks to its informal mathematical statement and literature anchor so an independent mathematician can check for definition drift, weakened hypotheses, or vacuity without reading proof internals.

> **Human review status:** Mechanical compilation, non-vacuity witnesses (`NonVacuity.lean`), and 6-kernel `lake comparator --paranoid` (for the 12 comparator targets in `lean/comparator.json` only) are automated. Rows were narrowed on 2026-11-26 to match an independent [statement audit](https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md). **Independent human line-by-line fidelity sign-off remains OPEN** (`human_line_by_line_review_recorded: false` in `formalization.yaml`).

| Track | Lean Declaration | Informal Claim | Literature Anchor | Fidelity Notes | Human Sign-Off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `HoggarBound.hoggar_bound` | $(D-1)\beta_6(S,f) \le (D-2)\lvert S\rvert\sqrt{(D-1)\lvert S\rvert}$ for any $N \ge 1$ Pauli subset $S$ (formalization of Jonah's prior result) | Jonah (Zenodo `23538829`, Oct 2026, unreviewed); Okumura (1974) | Uses explicit complex $2^N \times 2^N$ Pauli matrices (`Pauli.lean`) and operator-product signs (`lineSign`), no abstract oracle. Non-vacuity proved in `spectral_floor_nonvacuous`. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.hoggar_bound_quaternionic` | Kramers-doubled floor ($n = D/2$) on antiunitary-commuting sets & $Q^-(2N-1,2)$ (formalization of Jonah's prior result) | Jonah (Zenodo `23538829`); Muller et al. (`arXiv:2407.02928`) | Explicitly constructs $\theta^2 = -1$ commutation condition `qform u + symp w u = 0`. Non-vacuity: `kramers_nonvacuous`. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.mermin_peres`, `degree_three_qubit`, `degree_three_qubit_elliptic` | Exact degrees $d(Q^+(3,2))=1$, $d(W(5,2))=63$, $d(Q^-(5,2))=9$ (known values, formalized; not comparator targets) | Mermin (1990); Muller et al. (`arXiv:2407.02928`); Jonah (`23538829`) | Lower bound from `hoggar_bound`/`Kramers`; upper bound by explicit witness evaluated via kernel `decide +kernel` (zero `native_decide`). | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.saturation_tfae`, `saturation_mul_isSquare` | Floor saturation $\iff$ flat pure state on $S$, forcing $(2^N-1)\lvert S\rvert=\square$ | Unified paper Sec. 4; Cieśliński (`arXiv:2610.07172`) | Exact operator identity on `opA S f ^ 2`; non-vacuity: `saturation_tfae_nonvacuous`. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.NormPhaseFamily.infinite_nonclosed_saturated_family` | Infinite family of non-closed CCZ sets $\lvert\Psi_{3m}\rangle$ attaining the floor for all $m \ge 1$; contextual for $m \ge 2$ (degree 0 at $m = 1$) | Unified paper Thm 13b (new to bounded literature search; question posed in this manuscript) | Proves non-closure (`u + v ∉ S`), exact size $(q^3-1)q^2$, context count, lower bound, and attaining assignment for all $m \ge 1$; positivity of the degree (`infinite_nonclosed_family_contextual`) assumes $m \ge 2$. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.C3ExactOptima.corollary16_exact_binary_optima` | Four-qubit C3 binary optima for one fixed sign pair: $368$ ($\sigma_0$) vs $344$ ($\sigma_1$); cospectrality of the pair is in `C3Certificate.lean` / `C3Theorem.lean`, not compiled by CI at `v3.1.0` | Jonah (Zenodo `23524332`, unreviewed); Unified paper Thm 16'' | Pure-integer MET-SDP dual certificates (421/442 frustrated-triangle cuts) + explicit attaining binary vectors; zero floating point. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.C3AllQubits.c3_strict_law_fails_general`, `c3_all_qubits_completion` | All-qubit Case C3 explicit carrier family separating completion spectra for every $N \ge 4$ | Jonah (Zenodo `23524332`, unreviewed); Unified paper Thm 17 | Constructs explicit carrier pairs directly on the $N$-qubit hyperbolic quadric section (`CarrierFamily.lean`) and proves cospectral carriers with distinct completion cubic traces for all $N \ge 4$. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.ConjectureE.jonah_conjecture_e_all_nine_cases`, `AuditUpgrades.jonah_conjecture_e_all_nine_cases_spectra` | Strict-law failure for one explicit representative $(X,d)$ of each of the 9 vertex cases of Jonah's Conjecture E, every $N \ge 4$ | Jonah (Zenodo `23524332`, unreviewed, AI-refereed; C1 and C6 already proved there) | Constructs one explicit pair per case on `allPoints`, `quadric`, `perpSet`, separating both `charpoly` and canonical Hermitian eigenvalue multisets. *Caveats:* case labels are comments only, so case membership is read off the source's tables; transport to every hyperplane of a case uses cited Theorem B4 of Jonah [J3] outside Lean. | Open |
| 1 | `HoggarBound.ExactDegreesN4N5.w72_ge_1455`, `q9plus_ge_6444`, `exact_degrees_n4_n5_of_q7minus_315` | Lower bounds $1455$, $6444$ (independent of the census), CSS witnesses $(315,1575,6975)$, reduction to $d(Q^-(7,2)) \ge 315$ | Jonah (Zenodo `23510634`, unreviewed; earlier claimed the exact values $1575$, $6975$); Li–Gupta–Ganesh (`arXiv:2610.26465`); Muller et al. (`arXiv:2407.02928`) | Symplectic transvection invariance + double-counting proved in Lean; the 42-orbit `W(5,2)` census establishing $d(Q^-(7,2)) \ge 315$ is C11 + integer Python outside Lean. | Open |
| 2 | `ContextualityTensor.square_minimum_closed_form`, `pentagram_minimum_closed_form`, `global_actual_*` | Exact degrees $(7^k-5^k)/2$ ($k$ disjoint squares) and $(6^k-4^k)/2$ ($k$ pentagrams) for the explicit union-context family; answers the Sec. 6 stacking-limit question for these two families only | **Muller & Saniga (`arXiv:2609.19862v1`, Sec. 6, unreviewed preprint)**; context-count formula from their Sec. 4.2 | Full union context family (every nonempty choice of $\le 1$ local context per block) on disjoint observable vertices; exact evenness $2d_k = 7^k - 5^k$ (and $6^k - 4^k$) is proved in $\mathbb{Z}$ (`square_exact_degree`, `pentagram_exact_degree`) before dividing by $2$ (zero `Nat`-division truncation ambiguity); attaining witnesses are built into the theorem statements (non-vacuity). Literal Pauli matrices appear in `PhysicalBridge.lean` for two squares only; the pentagram has no Pauli realisation in Lean. No Lean theorem identifies the hard-coded seed lines with $HS(L(K_{3,3}))$ or $HS(\mathrm{Petersen})$ (Python enumeration). Comparator targets 9–10 use the tuple-indexed model; the limit theorems are standard-kernel only. | Open |
| 3 | `Evidence.sharp_minimum`, `success_upper_bound`, `BetTree.finite_hitting_bound`, `concrete_classical_false_positive` | Sharp Peres-Mermin setting-bias floor $\min_c p(c)$, finite adaptive-tree bound $\le z/T$, 36-round naive attack $>4.3\%$ (formalization of elementary bounds; finite form of Ville's inequality) | Peres (1990); Mermin (1990); Zhang–Glancy–Knill (2011); `papers/sequential-evidence/PRIOR_ART.md` | Formalized over exact finite binary trees with real probabilities; attaining witness is built into `sharp_minimum` and `concrete_classical_false_positive` constructs a concrete valid `BetTree` witness (non-vacuity); physical conditional-floor assumption is an explicit hypothesis, not verified by transcripts alone. | Open |
